The '''2025–26 season''' was the 144th season in the history of [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur Football Club]], their 48th consecutive season in the top flight of [[English football league system|English football]], and 34th consecutive season in the [[Premier League]]. In addition to the [[2025–26 Premier League|domestic league]], the club also participated in the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], and made a debut appearance in the [[2025 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]], with the latter two qualifications coming by virtue of winning the [[2025 UEFA Europa League final|UEFA Europa League final]] 1–0 against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[2024–25 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|previous season]].

The club endured a historically awful season on the pitch, finishing 17th in the Premier League for the second consecutive season. Tottenham were very close to being relegated, ultimately edging out London rivals [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] for survival by just two points. Early eliminations from all the cup competitions in conjunction with the league finish ensured Spurs for the [[2026–27 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2026–27 season]] would not play in any [[UEFA]]-sanctioned competition for the first time since the [[2023–24 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2023–24 season]] and only the third time since the [[2004–05 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2004–05 season]].

==Season summary==
Prior to the season, [[Thomas Frank (football manager)|Thomas Frank]] was headhunted from [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] and appointed as head coach on a three-year contract, replacing the sacked [[Ange Postecoglou]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Mokbel |first=Sami |date=6 June 2025 |title=Ange Postecoglou: Tottenham boss leaves 16 days after Europa League triumph |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c391v08kp9ro |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas Frank joins as Head Coach |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/june/thomas-frank-joins-as-head-coach/ |access-date=12 June 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=12 June 2025}}</ref> The summer transfer window also saw a significant leadership shift on the pitch, as long-serving captain [[Son Heung-min]] departed for [[Los Angeles FC]] after a decade at the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=LAFC Signs Global Football Icon Son Heung-Min |url=https://www.lafc.com/news/lafc-signs-global-football-icon-son-heung-min |date=6 August 2025 |access-date=25 May 2026 |publisher=Los Angeles FC}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=6 August 2025 |title=Son Heung-min: Tottenham forward joins LAFC in permanent move |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/clyrqzjj8ypo |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> This period of transition reached the boardroom on 4 September 2025, when [[Daniel Levy (businessman)|Daniel Levy]] resigned (but was widely understood to be ''de facto'' sacked by the Lewis Family) as executive chairman after nearly 25 years at the helm, with the Lewis Family citing a lack of footballing success and focus on football.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pitt-Brooke |first=Jack |date=26 September 2025 |title=How Tottenham sacked Daniel Levy – and how they've filled the void in the weeks since |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6661856/2025/09/26/how-tottenham-sacked-daniel-levy-and-how-they-filled-the-void-in-the-weeks-since/ |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c9qng2rj38do |title=Levy exits role as Tottenham executive chairman |work=BBC Sport |date=4 September 2025 |access-date=6 September 2025}}</ref>

The season started positively, with a competitive performance in the [[2025 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] against heavy favourites and European champions [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], albeit with Tottenham ultimately throwing away a 2–0 lead late on to draw 2–2 and losing on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]].<ref>{{cite web |title=PSG vs Tottenham LIVE: European Champions beat Spurs on penalties to win Super Cup |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cjr1l8epz02t |date=13 August 2025 |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Frank also won his first two league games, including a marquee win over [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] away from home, and Spurs were third in the league on [[Halloween]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Manchester City vs Tottenham Hotspur match report |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd0d3zjj8g3t |date=23 August 2025 |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=11v11 league table generator |url=https://www.11v11.com/league-tables/premier-league/31-october-2025/ |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=11v11}}</ref> However, optimism dissipated quickly due to a collapse in form, poor performances in derby losses to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in November,<ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham 0–1 Chelsea: Joao Pedro scores winner as hosts booed off |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3dn1j7nn4zt |date=1 November 2025 |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal vs Tottenham LIVE: Premier League score, stats & updates from North London Derby |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c70j2y8pk44t |date=23 November 2025 |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> and growing concerns about a very defensive style of football creating very few chances.<ref>{{cite web |last=Irfan |first=Umir |date=26 November 2025 |title=Tottenham tactics: Should Spurs be worried about their attack this season? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cg4nlgyq510o |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Tweedale |first=Ali |date=3 November 2025 |title=Three Shots, 0.1 xG: Just How Bad Were Spurs Against Chelsea? |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/spurs-xg-chelsea-thomas-frank-creativity |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Opta Analyst}}</ref> Spurs also suffered a very large injury crisis throughout 2026, with parallels to the preceding two seasons.<ref>{{cite news |last=Harris |first=Jay |date=25 May 2026 |title=Tottenham must address 'astronomical' injury crisis, James Maddison says |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7306832/2026/05/25/tottenham-injuries-james-maddison/ |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=The New York Times |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> Spurs hurtled down the league and despite pleas for patience Frank grew increasingly unpopular. Tottenham board members [[Vinai Venkatesham]] and [[Johan Lange (football executive)|Johan Lange]], promoted to positions of power after Daniel Levy's exit, would face criticism for retaining Thomas Frank for too long. By February 2026, a 2–1 home loss to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] left Spurs in 16th place, prompting the club to dismiss Frank after only eight months in charge following exits from both domestic cup competitions.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–2 Newcastle United: Jacob Ramsey fires Newcastle to rare away win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c8j34dxdjket |date=10 February 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2026/february/club-statement-thomas-frank/ |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |title=Club Statement - Thomas Frank |date=11 February 2026 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/ckgzqdzz1zdo |title=Frank sacked by Spurs after eight months in charge |work=BBC Sport |first=Sami |last=Mokbel |date=11 February 2026 |access-date=11 February 2026}}</ref>

The subsequent managerial search saw [[Igor Tudor]] appointed on 17 February as interim head coach.<ref>{{cite news |title=Men's Head Coach Update – Igor Tudor |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2026/february/men-s-head-coach-update-igor-tudor/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260214124045/https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2026/february/men-s-head-coach-update-igor-tudor/ |archive-date=14 February 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Bloom |first=Ben |date=17 February 2026 |title=Who is Spurs' new head coach Igor Tudor? |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4592313/who-is-new-spurs-head-coach-igor-tudor-and-what-are-his-tactics |access-date=17 February 2026 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=13 February 2026 |title=Igor Tudor agrees deal to become Tottenham's interim boss |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cvg87wlv7lmo |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Tudor was known for overseeing immediate upturns in results upon joining new clubs,<ref>{{cite news |date=13 February 2026 |title=Igor Tudor: Who is Tottenham's interim head coach? The former Juventus, Lazio, Marseille boss analysed |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13507144/igor-tudor-who-is-tottenhams-interim-head-coach-the-former-juventus-lazio-marseille-boss-analysed|work=Sky Sports}}</ref> yet his stint began with disastrous results, suffering losses to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in the league. His only other league game was a late-earned draw away at [[Anfield]] against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool 1–1 Tottenham Hotspur: Richarlison earns Spurs vital point |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c05vqzv88jnt |date=15 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> He also oversaw a 7–5 Champions League round of 16 aggregate loss to [[Atlético Madrid]], beginning with a 5–2 defeat in Spain, including being 4–0 down after 23 minutes due to goals from poor slips and individual errors.<ref>{{cite web |title=Keeper Kinsky substituted after only 17 minutes as Spurs collapse at Atletico |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cwyxjw5qvzqt |date=10 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Tudor played backup goalkeeper [[Antonín Kinský (footballer, born 2003)|Antonín Kinský]] in the match, but substituted him after sixteen minutes following two individual errors to much criticism.<ref>{{cite web |title=Antonin Kinsky: Spurs replace keeper after conceding three goals inside 15 minutes |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cly18g0lym4o |date=10 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Tottenham and Antonin Kinsky humiliated in Atletico Madrid defeat as Igor Tudor hits embarrassing Spurs low |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13518035/tottenham-and-antonin-kinsky-humiliated-in-atletico-madrid-defeat-as-igor-tudor-hits-embarrassing-spurs-low |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260311210933/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13518035/tottenham-and-antonin-kinsky-humiliated-in-atletico-madrid-defeat-as-igor-tudor-hits-embarrassing-spurs-low |date=11 March 2026 |archive-date=11 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Igor Tudor slammed for Antonin Kinsky treatment after early substitution in Atletico Madrid nightmare - 'Man management at its very worst' |url=https://www.tntsports.co.uk/football/champions-league/2025-2026/joe-hart-flabbergasted-by-igor-tudor-management-of-antonin-kinsky-steve-mcmanaman-says-man-management-at-its-very-very-worst_sto23279663/story.shtml |date=10 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |website=TNT Sports}}</ref>

Tudor was sacked as interim head coach on 29 March after just 44 days in charge, in the aftermath of a 3–0 home defeat to Nottingham Forest.<ref>{{cite web |last=Text |first=Live |title=Tottenham 0–3 Nottingham Forest: Spurs edge closer to the Championship after Morgan Gibbs-White scores |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c3wlw8zyvw6t |date=22 March 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=29 March 2026 |title=Club statement – Igor Tudor |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/1017865/club-statement-igor-tudor |access-date=25 May 2026 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cz0g57p8512o |work=BBC Sport |title=Tudor leaves Spurs after just 44 days in charge |first1=Jack |last1=Skelton |first2=Harry |last2=Poole |date=29 March 2026 |access-date=29 March 2026}}</ref> He was replaced by [[Roberto De Zerbi]], coming in as permanent manager.<ref>{{cite news |date=31 March 2026 |title=Roberto De Zerbi joins as Men's Head Coach |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/1018014/roberto-de-zerbi-joins-as-mens-head-coach |access-date=25 May 2026 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> The club's situation worsened on 10 April, when a 4–0 victory for [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] pushed Tottenham into the relegation zone after three or more games played for the first time since [[2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|January 2009]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Jess |title=Premier League LIVE: Build up to West Ham United vs Wolves: updates, scores, preview, team news, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c7vq1njv5gdt |date=10 April 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=10 April 2026 |title=Spurs drop into relegation zone for first time in 17 years as West Ham win |url=https://talksport.com/football/4176807/tottenham-relegation-zone-west-ham-premier-league/ |access-date=10 April 2026 |website=talkSPORT}}</ref> This standing served as the backdrop for De Zerbi's managerial debut two days later, which resulted in a 1–0 defeat at [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sunderland 1–0 Tottenham: De Zerbi's Spurs reign starts with defeat at Sunderland |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c4gv3232l14t |date=12 April 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

De Zerbi would go on to lead Spurs to eleven points from their final six matches, which would be enough to clinch safety on the final day and finish 17th. Tottenham went into the last game of the season knowing that only a loss at home to [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and a win for West Ham at home against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] would see them relegated, excluding an unrealistic twelve goal difference swing. Tottenham won 1–0; a [[João Palhinha]] goal in the 43rd minute from a corner was the winner.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham Hotspur vs Everton: Premier League preview, team news, stats & head-to-head |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5y7qyg03v7t |date=24 May 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> West Ham were therefore relegated despite a 3–0 win over Leeds.<ref>{{cite web |title=West Ham 3–0 Leeds - Hammers relegated despite final-day win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c70vr05gwelt |date=24 May 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

Despite confirming safety, the season would be remembered as one of the worst in Tottenham's history; the team had a historically close brush with relegation, three managers in a season, the large Champions League round of 16 first leg loss to Atlético Madrid, and were knocked out of the FA Cup in the third round for only the second time in twenty years, being eliminated by [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].<ref>{{cite news |date=8 January 2006 |title=Leicester 3-2 Tottenham |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/4565028.stm |access-date=25 May 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=3 January 2014 |title=Arsenal 2-0 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25531860 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham 1–2 Aston Villa: FA Cup defeat piles pressure on Spurs boss Thomas Frank |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/czx1d5k5gdkt |date=10 January 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> The Premier League finish of 17th meant that it was the first time Tottenham had finished as low as 17th in the top flight two years running for 111 years.<ref>{{cite web |last=Barker |first=Josh |date=21 May 2026 |title=Tottenham are set to match unwanted 111-year record even if they beat Everton |url=https://tbrfootball.com/tottenham-are-set-to-match-unwanted-111-year-record-even-if-they-beat-everton/ |access-date=25 May 2026 |website=TBR Football}}</ref> The club also lost six matches in a row across all competitions for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite web |date=10 March 2026 |title='Everything wrong' as Tottenham lose historic 6th in a row |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/48167923/tottenham-lose-historic-6th-straight |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=ESPN}}</ref> Tottenham did not win any of their first fifteen league games of 2026, the second-longest league winless streak in their history (sixteen games without a win in 1934–35).<ref>{{cite web |title=Tottenham 2–2 Brighton: Spurs' Premier League survival hopes dealt late blow by Seagulls |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c624d23p4d5t |date=18 April 2026 |access-date=26 May 2026 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref> Spurs also experienced historically poor home form, with only three home league wins all season, the joint-lowest by any Premier League team to escape relegation along with [[2008–09 Hull City A.F.C. season|Hull City in 2008–09]], including a run of one home win in seventeen.<ref>{{cite web |last=Ridge |first=Patric |date=24 May 2026 |title=Tottenham 1-0 Everton Stats: Spurs Survive on Final Day as Palhinha Earns Rare Home Win |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/tottenham-vs-everton-stats-opta-premier-league-final-day-05-2026 |access-date=26 May 2026 |website=Opta Analyst}}</ref> Everton were the only team Tottenham beat home and away in the league.

The season was considered by many to be the only serious threat of relegation experienced by a "[[Big Six (Premier League)|Big Six]]" club since the formation of the concept when [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] were taken over in 2008.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 September 2008 |title=Man City buyers complete takeover |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/7628080.stm |work=BBC Sport |access-date=25 May 2026}}</ref> The story of the missteps by the club executives and management, which nearly led Tottenham to what would have been a historic relegation to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] for the first time in 49 years, became the dominant narrative across the Premier League for the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/05/25/tottenhams-deluded-executive-deserved-to-be-relegated/ |title=Tottenham's deluded board deserved to be relegated until De Zerbi saved them |first=Matt |last=Law |date=25 May 2026 |access-date=25 May 2026 |publisher=The Telegraph}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c5y7j7752ppo |title=Spurs survival celebrations can't disguise season of embarrassment |first=Phil |last=McNulty |work=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2026 |access-date=24 May 2026}}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
On 31 March, Tottenham announced a pre-season tour to [[Asia]] with a friendly confirmed against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in [[Hong Kong]], which was the first-ever [[North London derby]] outside of the [[United Kingdom]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Club announces pre-season tour fixture against Arsenal in Hong Kong |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/march/club-announces-pre-season-tour-fixture-against-arsenal-in-hong-kong/ |access-date=1 April 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=31 March 2025}}</ref> Tottenham then announced a return to [[South Korea]], to compete in the Coupang Play Series 2025 against [[Newcastle United]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Opponents confirmed for Coupang Play Series match in Korea|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/may/opponents-confirmed-for-coupang-play-series-match-in-korea/|access-date=27 May 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=27 May 2025}}</ref> And a trip to [[Germany]] to face [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] for the [[Telekom Cup]] was confirmed next.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs to face FC Bayern in pre-season |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/may/spurs-to-face-fc-bayern-in-pre-season/ |access-date=16 May 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=16 May 2025}}</ref> On 13 June, a fourth friendly was added against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs to face Luton Town in July |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/june/spurs-to-face-luton-town-in-july/ |access-date=13 June 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=13 June 2025}}</ref> Two weeks later, a trip to [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] was announced.<ref>{{cite news |title=Reading trip added to pre-season schedule |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/june/reading-trip-added-to-pre-season-schedule/ |access-date=2 July 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=27 June 2025}}</ref>

A [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind-closed-doors]] friendly against [[Wycombe Wanderers F.C.|Wycombe Wanderers]] was also later announced.<ref>{{cite news |title=Further pre-season match scheduled for Saturday |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2025/july/further-pre-season-match-scheduled-for-saturday/ |access-date=23 July 2025 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur FC |date=23 July 2025}}</ref>
